title: Apartment Gym Emergency Preparedness Workout
author: Kyle
desc:
## Purpose

Build practical strength, endurance, carrying capacity, and general work capacity for emergency situations using equipment commonly available in an apartment gym.

Priorities:

- Lift, carry, push, and pull useful loads.
- Walk for extended periods without excessive fatigue.
- Climb stairs and hills efficiently.
- Develop single-leg strength, balance, grip, and trunk stability.
- Maintain useful strength while improving overall fitness.

The goal is practical physical capability rather than maximizing individual lifts.

---

## Equipment Used

- Fixed barbells
- Dumbbells
- Cable machine
- Adjustable benches
- Treadmill
- Stair climber
- Open space for loaded carries

---

## Warm-Up

Before each strength workout:

- Walk easily on the treadmill for 5 min.
- Use a comfortable pace.
- Keep the effort around RPE 2-3.
- Use the warm-up to raise body temperature and loosen the legs and ankles before lifting.

---

## Weekly Schedule

Use a repeating two-week schedule.

### Week 1

- Monday: Strength A
- Tuesday: Endurance
- Wednesday: Strength B
- Thursday: Hills and Stairs
- Friday: Strength A
- Saturday: Optional easy walk
- Sunday: Rest

### Week 2

- Monday: Strength B
- Tuesday: Endurance
- Wednesday: Strength A
- Thursday: Hills and Stairs
- Friday: Strength B
- Saturday: Optional easy walk
- Sunday: Rest

---

## Progression

### Strength A and Strength B

Use the listed rep and RPE ranges to determine load.

- Top of the rep range at the low end of the RPE range: increase weight next workout.
- Within the rep and RPE ranges: keep the weight and try to add reps over time.
- Bottom of the rep range at the top of the RPE range: keep the weight.
- Unable to reach the minimum reps without exceeding the RPE range: reduce weight.

Example for `3 x 6-10 @ RPE 7-8`:

- `3 x 10 @ RPE 7`: Increase weight.
- `3 x 8 @ RPE 7-8`: Keep weight and build reps.
- `3 x 6 @ RPE 8`: Keep weight.
- Cannot complete `3 x 6` without exceeding RPE 8: Reduce weight.

For carries, increase duration toward the top of the prescribed range before increasing weight.

### Endurance

Progress duration before speed or incline.

- Build from 35-40 min toward 60 min.
- Once the target duration is comfortable, gradually increase pace or incline.
- Change only one variable at a time.
- Keep most work at RPE 3-4 and conversational.

### Hills and Stairs

Progress stair-climber duration before increasing intensity.

- Gradually increase from 5-8 min toward 15-20 min.
- Keep the effort around RPE 3-4.
- Increase duration only when the current workload feels controlled.
- Use the treadmill portion for additional easy-to-moderate aerobic work.

### General Rule

Progress only when technique remains controlled and the prescribed RPE is maintained. If form deteriorates, pain develops, or the target intensity is exceeded, maintain or reduce the workload.

ex.note: Rest 90 sec. Use a comfortable depth and keep the movement controlled.
Rest 90-120 sec. Start standing. Slight knee bend, push hips back, keep dumbbells close to legs, and stop at a comfortable depth. Do not touch the floor between reps.

ss.note: Rest 90 sec. Keep feet planted, shoulder blades set, and lower the dumbbells under control. Press without bouncing or forcing shoulder range.
Rest 75-90 sec. Brace your trunk, pull toward the lower ribs, and control the return. Avoid leaning back to finish the rep. Flat back and bend to horizontal with the floor.

ex.note: Walk at RPE 3-4 and a conversational pace. Start around 2.4-2.7 mph and 0-1% incline. Progress duration before speed or incline.
Rest 60-90 sec. Hold dumbbells at your sides. Drive through the working leg, minimize push-off from the trailing foot, and control the descent. Use a comfortable step height.
Rest 90 sec. Hold a stable support, use a comfortable stance and depth, and keep the movement controlled.

ss.note: Rest 75-90 sec. Keep elbows slightly bent and ribs controlled. Lower the dumbbell behind your head to a comfortable stretch, then pull it back over your chest.
Rest 45-60 sec. Stand tall, brace your trunk, press straight out, and resist rotation. Use a load that lets you stay square to the cable.
Rest 90 sec. Sit supported, brace your trunk, press overhead under control, and stop short of any painful shoulder or back position.
Rest 60-90 sec. Brace one hand on the bench, keep your torso stable, pull the dumbbell toward the hip, and lower it under control.
